relationships.subject: TRPV1+ sensory neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: Thus, TRPV1 drugs alter core body temperature by modulating sensory input to the central nervous system, rather than through peripheral actions on the vasculature.

relationships.subject: capsaicin
relationships.evidence_quote: Strikingly, this capsaicin-evoked hypothermic response was completely abolished in sensory neuron-specific knockouts (PirtCre;Trpv1fl/fl)

relationships.subject: AMG517
relationships.evidence_quote: Indeed, AMG517 elicited a characteristic hyperthermia in control animals (as in human clinical trials), reaching a peak of ~0.5°C within 2 hr after injection (cf. Garami et al., 2010).

relationships.subject: CGRP
relationships.evidence_quote: suggesting that peripheral CGRP release from TRPV1+ nociceptors is largely dispensable in this drug-mediated thermomodulatory process, consistent with a centrally mediated mechanism.

key_findings: Deleting TRPV1 in sensory neurons, but not vascular smooth muscle, abolished capsaicin-induced hypothermia and AMG517-induced hyperthermia.
Ablating central projections of TRPV1+ DRG neurons reduced the thermal effects of TRPV1 drugs, whereas CGRP knockout had no effect.
